# 0.19.0 — 29 October 2026

Minor release on 0.18.0. The language server and its query engine, from [opentidehq/language-server 0.6.0](https://github.com/opentidehq/language-server/releases/tag/v0.6.0), are compiled into opentide: no extra, no second package. `validate` now checks every rule query offline, `lint` checks query style, `opentide lsp start` serves editors, and `opentide query` runs a query on a tenant. A query the platform would reject now fails `validate`, and wheels are built per platform.

## Upgrade

```bash
pip install opentide==0.19.0
export OPENTIDE_REPO_ROOT=/path/to/detection-repo
opentide validate --strict              # now also checks every rule query
opentide generate schemas               # the language server's catalogs
```

| Before | Now |
|--------|-----|
| `validate` passed a rule whose query the platform would reject | `validate` fails it (exit `1`); `--queries warn` reports it as a warning while you fix it, `--queries off` skips queries |
| `validate query` without `--live` exited `2` | it checks every rule query offline; `--live` is unchanged and still needs `--platform` |
| `--strategy` / `--wide` on `validate query` without `--live` | exit `2`: they choose tenants, so they need `--live` |
| `pip install opentide` installed a pure-Python wheel | one wheel per platform (Linux x86_64/arm64 glibc and musl, macOS Intel and Apple silicon, Windows x64, CPython 3.10+); elsewhere, including free-threaded Python, pip builds from the sdist and needs a Rust toolchain |
| Elastic advisories named by log events (`elastic_lookback_long_warning`) | the elastic-1.0 codes (`lookback_long`, `threshold_lookback`, `risk_band`, ...) |

## Added

- **The analysis engine ships with opentide** ([#332](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/332)): KQL (Sentinel and Defender), SPL, ES|QL, EQL, Kibana KQL, Lucene and Carbon Black's Lucene, and Tide objects, checked offline.
- **`opentide validate` checks queries by default** and **`opentide lint` checks query style** ([#685](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/685)); `validate query --file` takes query files.
- **`opentide lsp start`** serves the language server protocol for editors; **`opentide tui`** shows what it reports for each object.
- **`opentide query`** runs a read-only query on a platform's tenants and returns the rows ([#665](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/665)); MCP `run_query` and `DetectionRule.run_query` do the same.
- **`opentide deploy` reports each rule as it is sent** and counts every run, failed ones too ([#675](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/675)).
- **opentide checks objects with its own catalog** per schema revision ([#676](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/676), [#677](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/677)), and CI fails when the engine's bundled catalog is stale ([#679](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/679)).
- **`opentide explain`** pages for every engine code; **`opentide doctor`** checks the engine and the language-server catalogs; MCP `validate_query` checks offline.

## Changed

- **Elastic advisories use the platform specification's codes** ([#637](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/issues/637)).
- **A real deploy prints the plan** before it sends anything, and its outcome line always counts `failed` and `not attempted`.
- **Wheels are per platform**; the engine builds from crates.io (language-server 0.6.0).

See the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md) for every change.

## Verify

```bash
pip install opentide==0.19.0
python -c "import opentide; print(opentide.__version__)"   # 0.19.0
opentide doctor                                             # analysis_engine: language server 0.6.0
```
